DTR · TALK ABOUT A SCENE

Grandma Stitched the Script

STS-HS12-L3-BR300-HSVPAMA1112-CSR-AAD-02 • HS Media Arts Grades 11–12 • Technical Skills, Tools, and Conventions
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
Black quilters have told stories in quilts for generations, one scene in each square, like Harriet Powers did in Georgia in the 1880s. This quilt tells an Anansi story, a tale that began with the Akan people of Ghana and crossed the ocean to Jamaica. The clever spider hides all the world's wisdom in a pot, but the pot breaks and everyone gets a piece. Now the class is retelling the four quilt squares as six storyboard panels for a film.
The quilt has four squares, but the storyboard has six. Which moment would you film as a close-up shot, and why?
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
1
What is Aaliyah doing?
Look at the picture. Say: Aaliyah is ____. She makes panel ____. (drawing / eating) (six / one)
2
What is Desmond holding?
Look at the picture. Say: Desmond has ____. It is for the ____. (a spider puppet / a ball) (film / lunch)
3
What is the teacher doing?
Look at the picture. Say: The teacher is ____. He checks the ____. (watching / reading) (shot / mail)
4
What place is this? How do you know?
Look at the picture. Say: This is a ____. I see ____. (backyard / classroom) (a fence / desks)
5
Tell me about the storyboard.
Look at the picture. Say: The storyboard has ____. It plans the ____. (six drawings / six maps) (film / dinner)
6
What is Nia wearing?
Look at the picture. Say: Nia wears ____. She is ____. (an orange hoodie / a white shirt) (filming / sleeping)
Record an answer for each question, then submit.
